title: Update: Man shot by police in Kingsland has died from his injuries
article: A man shot by police following a chaotic confrontation at a Kingsland apartment building Saturday has died.
Deputy police chief Bob Ritchie described the incident as "one of the most difficult situations imaginable," and one that "required the use of lethal force."
"All members involved in this incident have the full and unequivocal support of the service and the executive," Ritchie said at a news conference Sunday morning.
Police arrived shortly after 9 p.m. after neighbours reported a man "yelling, screaming and throwing things" into the hallway of the second floor of Grandell Manor on 68th Avenue S.W.
Officers tried negotiating with the man - who had barricaded himself in his apartment - but after about 30 minutes, Ritchie said, the situation took a violent turn.
"The man jumped from a second-storey balcony and confronted officers," he said. "At approximately 9:30 p.m., an officer-involved shooting occurred."
The man, who was in his 40s, died around 2:30 a.m. after being rushed to Foothills Hospital in life-threatening condition.
Ritchie confirmed that weapons were recovered from the scene.
A message that the Calgary Police Association provided to its membership described the man as "armed with edged weapons," and said he "rushed one of the members."
"That member was forced to use his service pistol and was able to successfully stop the threat," CPA president Les Kaminski wrote to police rank and file.
Sources told Postmedia on Saturday that the man had threatened police with an axe.
The patrol officer involved is a 10-year veteran of the Calgary Police Service, Ritchie said.
"Our officers did their very best to de-escalate this situation, to use strategic communications throughout this and to engage this individual in different forms of communication," Ritchie said.
"Oftentimes, it's outside of the officers' ability to control that."
The man who was shot has no criminal history. And while he had "interactions" with police in the past, Ritchie said, they weren't criminal in nature.
One of the man's neighbours said she was awakened around 9 p.m. Saturday by screaming and yelling.
Trisha Brigden opened the door of her unit to see what appeared to be an air conditioning unit and a bunch of her neighbour's belongings strewn across the hallway.
"(He) kept banging on the door from the inside," Brigden said. "He was just going crazy in there."
Brigden said she had seen her neighbour a few hours earlier and he seemed fine. She said she believed he lived alone in the apartment.

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) is investigating. The officer involved will be placed on a 30-day leave before he'll be permitted to return to active duty, according to Calgary police.
This is the first officer-involved shooting in Calgary in 2018.
